precontact.note: Estimated 25,000-36,000 Cherokee across ~64 towns in five divisions

1777.note: Population halved by 1738 smallpox epidemic; further losses in Cherokee-American wars

1798.note: Population stable but land pressure increasing

1806.note: Cherokee adopting written laws, plantation agriculture

1814.note: Cherokee fought as U.S. allies at Horseshoe Bend; Jackson took their land anyway

1819.note: ~1,500-2,000 voluntarily emigrate west; Cherokee Council declares "not one more foot"

1835.note: Henderson Roll count: 16,542 Cherokee + 201 whites + 1,592 enslaved. Treaty of New Echota cedes ALL land.

removal.note: An estimated 2,000 to 4,000 died — in camps before the march, during the journey, and in the first year after arrival. Estimates vary (Mooney 1900: 4,000; Thornton 1984: up to 8,000 if post-arrival deaths counted; current scholarship: 2,000–4,000).

today.note: Cherokee Nation is the largest tribal nation in the United States
